title: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: New Mexico requires sellers of residential real property to provide a written disclosure statement to the buyer. The statement must cover structural, mechanical, environmental, and other known conditions including water damage, pest infestation, and known defects. Must be delivered before or at the time of contract execution.

required_actions.note: Failure to disclose known material defects may result in rescission or damages.

title: Brokerage Relationship Disclosure
description: New Mexico brokers must disclose their agency relationship at the first substantive contact. The Real Estate Commission requires written disclosure of the brokerage relationship type (exclusive buyer agency, exclusive seller agency, dual agency, or transaction broker). Dual agency requires written informed consent.

title: Community Property State — Spousal Consent
description: New Mexico is a community property state. Both spouses must sign the deed and related closing documents for the sale of community property, even if only one spouse is listed on title. Failure to obtain spousal consent may render the transaction voidable. Title companies must verify marital status during the closing process.

required_actions.note: Both spouses must sign the deed for community property transfers.
Title company must verify marital status and community property classification.

title: Closing Type — Title Company / Escrow
description: New Mexico residential closings are typically conducted by title companies or escrow agents. Attorney involvement is not required by statute. Title insurance is customary and is typically provided by a title company that also handles escrow and closing.

required_actions.note: Title company or escrow agent conducts closing. Attorney optional.

title: Water Rights Disclosure
description: New Mexico law requires disclosure of water rights associated with real property. Water is a critical and scarce resource in New Mexico, and water rights are severable from land ownership. Sellers must disclose any water rights appurtenant to the property, whether they are being transferred with the property, and any known impairments or restrictions on water use.

required_actions.note: Water rights may be severed from land. Buyer should verify with NM Office of the State Engineer.
